evidence: Cic. Div. 1.78: ut flūmina in contrāriās partēs flūxerint (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word for water, rivers and anything that flows; flūmen, “river”, is made from it.

evidence: Verg. A. 3.175: gelidus tōtō mānābat corpore sūdor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of liquid that seeps or trickles: sweat, tears, blood from the nose.

phrases.latin: stillicidium eō quod stillātim cadit; flūmen quod fluit continuē
phrases.english: the drip from the eaves (stillicidium) because it falls drop by drop (stillātim); a river (flūmen) because it flows on and on

phrases.latin: īnfīrmō capitī fluit ūtilis, ūtilis alvō
phrases.english: it flows, good for a weak head, good for the stomach

fluxi.claim: long u in the perfect and supine
fluxi.html: De Vaan s.v. fluō, after Weiss (1994), explains flūxī as made by analogy on struō : strūxī, which has a long vowel. The house spelling of the readers (latinitas AGENTS.md §2), with the compounds dēflūxit, efflūxit.

sources: Lewis & Short: fluo · Lewis & Short: mano
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), s.v. fluō.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-varro, loci-horatius), checked against the editions named there.
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
